title: Validation ranking hid one detector’s false positives on genuine photos
summary: An OpenCLIP detector selected at 98.43% validation accuracy flagged 1,143 of 5,413 genuine photographs in a held-out OpenForensics-derived test set. A checkpoint ranked lower on validation flagged 275 genuine images and missed more manipulated images. The test contained 10,905 images.
organization: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§IV-A, IV-C, IV-G–H, Tables III, V and IX, and V-D–G

evidence.tested: The validation-selected detector had 98.43% accuracy on validation and 88.85% on a 10,905-image held-out OpenForensics-derived test. Test errors included 1,143 false accusations among 5,413 genuine photographs. The final weight average, lower-ranked on validation, had 94.76% accuracy and 275 false positives but more missed manipulations.
evidence.unknown: The result comes from a single training run and two disjoint partitions of one derived corpus. The pattern is not independently replicated, and illustrative examples do not establish what caused the false positives.
evidence.ai_role: Fine-tuned OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 checkpoints classified genuine and manipulated photographs. The trained regular and averaged checkpoints could be compared on the same held-out classification set.
